title: The Search for the Wicked Witch, part 7
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: But Dorothy they did not harm at all. She stood, with Toto in her arms, watching the sad fate of her comrades and thinking it would soon be her turn. The leader of the Winged Monkeys flew up to her, his long, hairy arms stretched out and his ugly face grinning terribly; but he saw the mark of the Good Witch’s kiss upon her forehead and stopped short, motioning the others not to touch her.

“We dare not harm this little girl,” he said to them, “for she is protected by the Power of Good, and that is greater than the Power of Evil. All we can do is to carry her to the castle of the Wicked Witch and leave her there.”

So, carefully and gently, they lifted Dorothy in their arms and carried her swiftly through the air until they came to the castle, where they set her down upon the front doorstep. Then the leader said to the Witch:

“We have obeyed you as far as we were able. The Tin Woodman and the Scarecrow are destroyed, and the Lion is tied up in your yard. The little girl we dare not harm, nor the dog she carries in her arms. Your power over our band is now ended, and you will never see us again.”
Then all the Winged Monkeys, with much laughing and chattering and noise, flew into the air and were soon out of sight.

The Wicked Witch was both surprised and worried when she saw the mark on Dorothy’s forehead, for she knew well that neither the Winged Monkeys nor she, herself, dare hurt the girl in any way. She looked down at Dorothy’s feet, and seeing the Silver Shoes, began to tremble with fear, for she knew what a powerful charm belonged to them. At first the Witch was tempted to run away from Dorothy; but she happened to look into the child’s eyes and saw how simple the soul behind them was, and that the little girl did not know of the wonderful power the Silver Shoes gave her. So the Wicked Witch laughed to herself, and thought, “I can still make her my slave, for she does not know how to use her power.” Then she said to Dorothy, harshly and severely:

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what stopped the leader of the Monkeys from harming Dorothy?
options: The mark of the Good Witch's kiss on her forehead
The Silver Shoes she wore on her feet
The dog she was holding in her arms
An order shouted by the Witch herself

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Monkeys do with Dorothy instead?
options: Carried her gently to the Witch's castle doorstep
Left her standing where she was
Took her back towards the Emerald City
Set her down among the sharp rocks

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the leader tell the Witch?
options: That her power over their band was now ended
That they would serve her once more if asked
That the girl had been destroyed with the rest
That the Golden Cap had been lost

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what made the Witch begin to tremble?
options: The sight of the Silver Shoes on Dorothy's feet
The laughter of the departing Monkeys
The roar of the Lion in the yard
The mark upon Dorothy's forehead

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Witch finally speak to Dorothy?
options: Harshly and severely
Kindly and sweetly
In a trembling whisper
Not at all, at first

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the leader say they dare not harm her?
options: She is protected by a Power of Good greater than Evil
She has done the Monkeys no injury at all
The Witch had forbidden it in her order
She is too small to be worth the trouble

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Witch decide not to run away?
options: She saw the girl did not know the Shoes' power
She remembered the Monkeys would defend her
She was too proud to flee from a child
The Lion in the yard blocked her escape

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did Dorothy expect while she watched?
options: That her own turn would come soon
That the Monkeys would set her friends free
That the Witch would come out to meet her
That the Wizard would send help

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does motioning the others mean?
options: Signalling to them with a gesture
Shouting an order to them
Pushing them away with his arms
Flying ahead to lead them

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A mark of protection saves Dorothy, but leaves her the Witch's prisoner
The Monkeys turn on the Witch and free the travellers
Dorothy uses the Silver Shoes to escape the Monkeys
The Witch is destroyed by the power of the kiss

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Monkeys report about the Woodman and Scarecrow?
options: That they were destroyed
That they had escaped
That they were tied in the yard
That they had joined the Winkies

questions.prompt: Per the passage, where did the Monkeys set Dorothy down?
options: On the front doorstep of the castle
In the yard beside the Lion
In the castle kitchen
On the rocks where the Woodman fell

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Monkeys leave?
options: Laughing and chattering, into the air
Silently, one by one
Carrying the Golden Cap with them
Only after the Witch dismissed them

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did the leader look like as he flew at Dorothy?
options: Arms stretched out and his ugly face grinning
Small and frightened, hanging back
Wrapped in the coils of rope
Wearing the Witch's Golden Cap

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did the Witch know about the Silver Shoes?
options: That a powerful charm belonged to them
That they had been made for her
That they would melt in water
That only a witch could wear them

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that he stopped short?
options: He checked himself suddenly
He stopped only briefly
He fell to the ground
He called out a warning

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: Two protections save Dorothy, but leave her in the Witch's hands
The Witch is defeated by the Winged Monkeys she called up
Dorothy is destroyed along with the rest of her companions
The Monkeys carry Dorothy safely home again to Kansas
